text: a voice pitched low, the way a voice gets in a room rented by the hour
eyes that go to the door every time it opens, and come back slower each time
a matchbook turning end over end, never struck
counting the change twice before it goes in the pocket
talking with the chin down, the way people talk through a grille
a good coat two seasons old, cuffs turned once already
collar buttoned, no tie, and a smear of green paint at one shoulder
boots wet to the laces and dry everywhere above them
A scar through one eyebrow, thin as a pencil line.
Her left hand curled slightly, an old break that never set right.
A voice pitched low, like he'd learned to talk through a closed door.
Knuckles scarred white across every one, the marks of a bare-knuckle youth.
A gold tooth, upper left, that showed when he laughed.
Her eyes were two different shades of brown, close enough most men missed it.
A limp he covered by never standing still.
Fingers stained yellow to the second knuckle.
A widow's peak going gray at the edges first.
Her voice cracked on the high notes, like a girl's that never finished growing up.
A burn scar along one forearm, shaped like a flatiron pressed flat.
A left ear that sat lower than the right, from a fall as a boy.
Her hands shook faintly at rest, and steadied the moment she picked something up.
A jaw he held tight even when he wasn't angry.
Freckles across the bridge of her nose that face powder never quite covered.
A voice that dropped to a whisper mid-sentence, out of old habit.
Thick wrists, the kind that came from years hauling something heavy.
One eyebrow set permanently higher than the other.
A gap between her front teeth she'd stopped trying to hide.
Nails bitten to the quick on the right hand only.
A soft chin, younger-looking than the rest of him put together.
Her hair going white at one temple only, a streak an inch wide.
A boxer's flattened nose above a mild, apologetic mouth.
Hands too small for the rest of him, and he knew it.
A stare that didn't blink as often as it should.
A rasp in the voice, left over from a fever nobody named.
Long fingers, ink-stained at the first joint.
Her chin lifted a half-inch before she answered anything.
A birthmark the shape of a thumbprint, just under the left ear.
Eyes set close together under heavy brows.
A dimple that showed only on the left, even when he wasn't smiling.
Her wedding band worn thin on the underside, the only soft metal on her.
A crooked little finger, broken once and never reset.
Skin gone leathery at the throat from years outdoors.
A voice pitched for a bigger room than the one she stood in.
Eyebrows plucked to two thin arches, drawn back in with a pencil.
A front tooth chipped at an angle, never capped.
Hands that stayed folded, like they'd learned not to be seen fidgeting.
A neck too thick for his collar, whatever collar he wore.
Pale eyes that looked paler for how dark her hair was.
A stammer that only showed on words starting with a hard C.
Earlobes pierced twice on the left, once on the right.
A squint that came from reading in bad light for thirty years.
A jaw scar shaped like a fishhook, just under the ear.
Hands as soft as a boy's, on a man past fifty.
A voice that rose at the end of every sentence, like every fact was a question.
One shoulder set lower, from carrying a bag the same way for years.
A trace of an accent that came out only on numbers.
Grey eyes that went nearly black when the light dropped.
A callus in the web of the thumb, the width of a rope.
Taps two fingers on the table before answering anything.
Chews the same toothpick down to a sliver.
Counts change twice, out loud, before pocketing it.
Cracks each knuckle in order, left hand first.
Rolls a coin across his fingers when he's thinking.
Straightens picture frames that are already straight.
Folds her handkerchief into smaller and smaller squares.
Polishes his glasses on his tie, though the lenses never look any cleaner.
Hums the same four notes whenever the questions get close.
Chews her lower lip until it colors.
Taps ash before there's any ash to tap.
Straightens his tie by feel, never checking a glass.
Licks a thumb before turning any page.
Adjusts cufflinks that don't need adjusting.
Clears his throat before every lie, and some of the truths too.
Twists a ring around and around without taking it off.
Snaps a rubber band against the wrist.
Picks lint off a sleeve that has none.
Bites the inside of her cheek instead of answering right away.
Drums a march rhythm nobody else hears.
Sniffs the air before answering, like checking for something burning.
Pats a breast pocket to confirm what's already there.
Tugs an earlobe when a question lands close to home.
Blinks hard, twice, before saying a name out loud.
Straightens a stack of papers that's already square.
Runs a thumbnail along the seam of the table.
Sighs through the nose instead of the mouth.
Cracks his neck to one side before speaking.
Wipes the same rail with the same rag whether it needs it or not.
Rubs at a wedding band that isn't there anymore.
Clicks a pen open and shut, open and shut.
Straightens a hat that's already straight.
Sucks air through the teeth before a hard answer.
Picks at a hangnail through the whole conversation.
Repeats the last word of a question back before answering it.
Shifts weight foot to foot like the floor is cold.
Taps a cigarette against the case three times before lighting it.
Smooths her skirt over her knees, though it's already smooth.
Rolls the shoulders like a coat that doesn't fit right.
Counts under the breath, one to five, before speaking.
Turns a glass in slow circles without drinking from it.
Picks a thread off a cuff, examines it, drops it.
Studies his own hands when a question gets personal.
Whistles two bars of the same tune between sentences.
Buttons and unbuttons the top button of a coat.
Wets a pencil tip with the tongue before writing.
Straightens a stack of coins into a column.
Cracks the knuckles of one hand, then presses them into the other palm.
Looks at the door before answering anything at all.
Tucks loose hair behind one ear, the same ear, every time.
A derby a size too small, worn anyway.
A fedora with the brim turned down against a rain that wasn't falling.
Spats gone gray at the toe from city slush.
A stickpin holding a tie that had seen better collars.
A boiled shirt with a ring of yellow at the collar.
A Norfolk jacket, belted, meant for a country he'd never visited.
A watch chain looped twice across the vest, no watch on the end of it.
A shirtwaist buttoned to the throat, regardless of the weather.
A cloche hat pulled low enough to shadow one eye.
Gaiters buttoned over shoes that didn't need them.
A topcoat with the lining coming loose at one cuff.
A slicker still dripping from a rain three blocks back.
Knickers gone through at one knee, mended with the wrong thread.
A mended glove, the left one, three stitches short of matching the right.
A pawned watch chain, bought back once and worn for the look of the thing.
A collar a half-size too tight, and he wouldn't loosen it.
A hat band dark with sweat under a fresh brim.
A coat with a torn pocket, sewn shut instead of mended.
Cuffs turned to hide the fray.
A vest buttoned one hole off, all evening, and nobody told him.
A tie held with a dime-store pin instead of the real thing.
A dress let out at the seams, the stitching newer than the fabric.
A coat two seasons out of style and brushed clean anyway.
Gloves kept on indoors, past any reasonable hour.
A hem taken up an inch, the old line still showing.
A collar starched hard enough to leave a mark on the throat.
Shoes resoled twice, shined enough to hide it.
A muffler wound twice around the neck, even indoors.
A brooch pinned slightly crooked, like it went on in a hurry.
A pocket square that didn't match anything else he had on.
A raincoat buttoned to the collar though the sky was clear.
A hat left on indoors, out of habit more than manners.
Cufflinks that didn't match, one plain, one carved.
A shawl worn indoors against a cold nobody else felt.
A skirt hemmed shorter than the fashion plates called for.
A jacket let out across the shoulders, tailored once for a heavier man.
Stockings with a run mended in ink instead of thread.
A necktie knotted too tight, like it went on in the dark.
A pair of galoshes left by the door, never quite dry.
A ring worn on a chain instead of a finger.
A handkerchief with an initial that wasn't his.
A coat collar turned up though the night was mild.
A garter showing for half a second, and never again.
Buttons that didn't match down one side of a coat.
A borrowed overcoat, sleeves an inch short.
A hat with a feather missing from the band.
A vest with a cigar burn patched over.
Shoes a half-size large, stuffed with newspaper at the toe.
A collar pin holding together what a missing button used to.
A bob cut close, with a shingle at the back nobody's caught up to yet.
